policy_version: NU Clark Student Handbook 2025 Edition with project operational definition dated 2026-08-01
positive_criteria: Deliberately organizing or participating in coordinated activity intended to violently overthrow or forcibly replace lawful school or government authority.
Recruiting, encouraging, or directing rebellion, sedition, extremist activity, or serious illegal action against the school or state.
Deliberately sabotaging critical school operations as part of an effort to threaten institutional safety or security or make lawful governance inoperative.
required_boundary: The narrative must contain evidence of deliberate intent plus coordinated, violent, seriously illegal, or security-threatening action aimed at lawful authority or institutional operations. Ordinary misconduct or violence alone is classified under its more specific handbook offense.
explicit_exclusions: Peacefully expressing opinions or criticizing school or government policies.
Participating in lawful student organizations or peaceful demonstrations that follow school rules.
Filing complaints, petitions, grievances, or reports of misconduct through proper channels.
Threats, fights, assault, disruption, vandalism, weapons, or computer breaches without the required subversive purpose; use the more specific handbook offense instead.
decision_boundary: The model only recommends MAJOR-30 for Discipline Office review and does not determine criminal liability, political affiliation, guilt, or sanctions.
